The dynamics of the 3-pendulum are governed by the Euler-Lagrange equations derived from the Lagrangian L = KE - PE, where positions and velocities are computed using the absolute angles theta_i from the downward vertical. With equal rod lengths L_i = 1 m and masses m_i = 1 kg, the kinetic energy leads to the mass matrix M(theta) as:

M = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2) & \cos(\theta_1 - \theta_3) \\ 2\cos(\theta_1 - \theta_2) & 2 & \cos(\theta_2 - \theta_3) \\ \cos(\theta_1 - \theta_3) & \cos(\theta_2 - \theta_3) & 1 \end{pmatrix}

The potential energy is V = -g (3 \cos\theta_1 + 2 \cos\theta_2 + \cos\theta_3).

The equations of motion are M \dot{\omega} = \tau_g + Q(\theta, \omega), where \tau_g = [-3g \sin\theta_1, -2g \sin\theta_2, -g \sin\theta_3]^T is the gravity torque vector, and Q contains the centrifugal and Coriolis terms obtained from \frac{1}{2} \sum_{ij} \omega_i \omega_j \frac{\partial M_{ij}}{\partial \theta_k} - \sum_{ij} \omega_i \omega_j \frac{\partial M_{kj}}{\partial \theta_i} for each k (no damping term since coefficient = 0).

This results in a system of 6 coupled nonlinear ODEs. Due to strong nonlinearity and chaos in triple pendulums, analytical solution is impossible, and accurate prediction requires numerical integration (e.g., RK4 or adaptive symplectic integrator with dt ≈ 0.001 s for stability over t=1 s, ~1000 steps).

Manual computation of hundreds of steps (including 3x3 matrix inversions, trig functions, etc.) is infeasible in text. Initial accelerations are O(10) rad/s² from gravity, with significant coupling from initial configuration (theta1 ≈ 106°, theta2 ≈ -47°, theta3 ≈ 91° mod 2π) and velocities O(1-2) rad/s, leading to substantial state evolution over 1 s.

As a first-order approximation ignoring accelerations (valid only for very short t), the state is theta(t) ≈ theta_0 + omega_0 t, omega(t) ≈ omega_0. This neglects ~O(t^2) changes but illustrates the motion trend.
